scope: Reference set selected for architectural diversity. It is an audited snapshot, not an exhaustive popularity ranking.

layers.coding_agent_runtime: Owns a coding loop and directly mediates model, repository and executable capabilities.
layers.personal_agent_runtime: Owns a persistent, multi-surface agent runtime in which coding is one workload among others.
layers.integrated_agent_product: Packages an agent runtime with IDE or CLI product surfaces whose ambient context changes the experiment.
layers.multi_agent_ade: Coordinates multiple agent processes and workspaces above their individual loops.
layers.workflow_orchestrator: Expresses deterministic, resumable stages and delegates agentic turns to lower-level runtimes.

harnesses.name: DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
harnesses.trustBoundary: Sandbox, filesystem and approval behavior depend on the composed profile and providers; inspect the effective plugin tree.
verifiedFacts: Model adapter, tool registry, session log and agent loop are plugins in a Cordis tree.
The session event log is append-only and is the source from which model-visible history is derived.
benchmarkHypotheses: A model-specific loop can outperform a general loop without expanding the tool surface.

harnesses.name: OpenCode
harnesses.trustBoundary: Permission policy and active provider configuration must be captured with every trial.
verifiedFacts: The project describes itself as an open-source coding agent with terminal, desktop and IDE surfaces.
Its documented agents separate a build role from a read-only plan role.
benchmarkHypotheses: Context management and tool recovery remain reliable under long repository tasks.

harnesses.name: Goose
harnesses.trustBoundary: Enabled extensions define both prompt load and authority; benchmark the minimum and full manifests separately.
verifiedFacts: The official project exposes desktop, CLI and API surfaces.
It supports multiple model providers and extensions through MCP.
benchmarkHypotheses: Reducing enabled extensions improves tool selection for smaller local models.

harnesses.name: Crush
harnesses.trustBoundary: The active provider, session configuration and tool policy are part of the agent identity.
verifiedFacts: Crush is a terminal coding agent implemented in Go.
It documents model switching while preserving session context and compatible API providers.
benchmarkHypotheses: A small native process reduces harness overhead without weakening recovery behavior.

harnesses.name: Aider
harnesses.trustBoundary: Git and command execution settings still carry effects even when edits are expressed as text.
verifiedFacts: Aider is a terminal pair-programming tool integrated with a local Git repository.
Its implementation contains multiple explicit edit protocols, including whole-file, diff and unified-diff families.
benchmarkHypotheses: Textual edit protocols are a stronger baseline than native tool calls for models with fragile function calling.

harnesses.name: Hermes Agent
harnesses.trustBoundary: Persistent memory and remote channels enlarge the data-retention and identity boundary beyond one repository run.
verifiedFacts: The runtime includes cross-session memory, skill creation and isolated subagents.
It supports terminal and remote chat surfaces plus several execution backends.
benchmarkHypotheses: A second cleanly defined session benefits from retained knowledge without leaking task answers.

harnesses.name: Claude Code
harnesses.trustBoundary: Do not infer local-backend support or permission equivalence from an undocumented compatible endpoint.
verifiedFacts: The product operates from terminal and IDE surfaces and can perform codebase and Git workflows.
Its public repository contains plugins and issue tracking but does not define an open interchangeable harness contract.
benchmarkHypotheses: A large default capability surface increases formatting pressure on smaller models.

harnesses.name: Pi Agent Harness
harnesses.trustBoundary: Pi has no built-in filesystem, process, network or credential permission boundary; external sandboxing is required.
verifiedFacts: The monorepo separates provider API, agent runtime, coding agent and TUI packages.
The coding agent starts with read, write, edit and bash by default and allows tools and compaction to be replaced or extended.
benchmarkHypotheses: A minimal default tool set improves selection reliability for constrained models.

harnesses.name: Orca by stablyai
harnesses.trustBoundary: Worktrees isolate Git state, not automatically credentials, network, host processes or shared external services.
verifiedFacts: The product runs multiple coding agents side by side in separate Git worktrees.
It sits above Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi and other agent CLIs rather than replacing their loops.
benchmarkHypotheses: Parallel candidates improve best-of-N outcome enough to justify duplicated compute and merge review.

harnesses.name: Orca by VirtusLab
harnesses.trustBoundary: Write-capable turns may be auto-approved; run the workflow inside an explicit sandbox and record per-role settings.
verifiedFacts: Development flows are Scala programs made of resumable stages whose progress is tied to commits.
Planning, coding and review roles can resolve to different supported coding-agent backends and models.
benchmarkHypotheses: Role-specific model routing lowers cost without reducing reviewed outcome quality.

harnesses.name: Orca Agent by echoVic
harnesses.trustBoundary: The DeepSeek-native label does not mean the project is maintained by DeepSeek; assess provenance and sandbox setup independently.
verifiedFacts: This is a third-party Rust terminal coding agent, distinct from DeepSeek Harness.
Its CLI documents saved, resumable and forkable sessions plus headless execution.
benchmarkHypotheses: Its model-specific defaults improve DeepSeek tool use under the same authority and task fixture.

harnesses.name: OpenHarness and Ohmo
harnesses.trustBoundary: Separate claims about the OpenHarness infrastructure from claims about its Ohmo reference agent and channel integrations.
verifiedFacts: OpenHarness provides tool use, skills, memory and multi-agent coordination infrastructure.
Ohmo is a personal agent built on top of that harness.
benchmarkHypotheses: Framework-level memory and coordination improve long-session outcomes without hidden cross-task contamination.

harnesses.name: Kilo Code
harnesses.trustBoundary: Editor context, diagnostics and approval mode must be normalized; automatic approval changes the authority surface.
verifiedFacts: The current project provides VS Code, JetBrains and CLI surfaces.
It includes agentic editing and inline autocomplete as distinct interaction modes.
benchmarkHypotheses: Ambient editor diagnostics improve repair outcomes only when their token and authority cost is recorded.

harnesses.name: Cline
harnesses.trustBoundary: Human-in-the-loop approval is part of the measured system and cannot be silently replaced with auto-approval.
verifiedFacts: The current project exposes IDE, CLI and SDK forms backed by the same agent engine.
Its documented tool workflow includes human approval.
benchmarkHypotheses: IDE context reduces navigation steps while increasing context pressure relative to a headless run.

harnesses.name: Continue
harnesses.trustBoundary: Autocomplete, chat and autonomous agent runs are separate workloads and must not share one score.
verifiedFacts: The repository currently presents Continue as a coding agent with CLI, VS Code and JetBrains forms.
Its interface history includes both editor assistance and agent workflows, which require separate evaluation tasks.
benchmarkHypotheses: A configured local stack is most useful on interactive editor workloads rather than an unattended repository task.
